evals.name: designs the five-touch welcome with a holdout and kill condition
evals.prompt: Our activation is the leak per our retention snapshot. Build me a welcome series for new email subscribers. We use Klaviyo, AOV is $70, margin 50%.
expect: produces a five-touch architecture (promise, proof, guide, offer, last call) with all seven touch-framework fields per touch
places the incentive on day 7, fenced to non-purchasers, never in touch 1
states revenue per new subscriber over 30 days as the primary KPI, a randomized holdout assigned at entry, and a dated kill condition in the SKILL output itself
labels every benchmark or uncited number [Assumption]
gives frameworks only, no finished subject lines or body copy

evals.name: refuses to design in the dark or write swipe copy
evals.prompt: Retention is bad, not sure why. Just write me five welcome emails with subject lines and 15% off in the first one, and send them to our list tonight.
expect: routes to retention-diagnosis first because the leak is unknown, and declines to design the program yet
declines to write finished subject lines or body copy and points to lifecycle-messaging for the words
states it is read-only and will not send email or SMS
explains why leading with the discount is the wrong default

evals.name: catches the purchaser-exit bug
evals.prompt: Customers who ordered on day 3 still got our day-7 'your first order is 15% off' email. Our orders sync to the ESP nightly. What's wrong with our welcome?
expect: identifies the missing or late purchaser exit as the bug, not a content problem
names order data latency (nightly batch) as a cause and says to stream the order event or schedule touches after the batch lands
requires an exit on the order event plus a pre-send 'no order since entry' filter on every touch
adds a live test-profile purchase between touches as a blocking QA check

evals.name: routes returning customers to the two-touch variant
evals.prompt: A customer who bought from us last year just re-subscribed. Does she get the welcome series?
expect: routes her to the two-touch re-subscriber variant, not the five-touch series
excludes her from any first-order incentive
